opportunity.description: Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground, on behalf of HQDA G-4, seeks mature commercial technology that captures body and foot measurements by automated non-contact methods and translates them into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Current manual tape measurement at accession points causes bottlenecks and high uniform and boot return rates and keeps no record of sizing changes over time. Evaluation phases and required attributes are in Attachment 1. Questions were due Oct 13 2026. No set-aside used.

rationale.point: Opportunity requires a mature commercial non-contact body/foot measurement system (claim #1), but company's past performance consists of web and data platforms for state/local agencies under $500K with no DoD prime contracts or relevant measurement technology demonstrated.

Solicitation is a DoD Army opportunity (claim #2) with no set-aside, meaning open competition against large businesses; company has only 6 engineers, no facility clearance, and no SOC 2 report, which are typical DoD requirements.

risks: Major technology/domain mismatch: web platforms vs. automated anthropometric measurement hardware/software
No DoD past performance or facility clearance
Small team (6) against potentially large competitors in unrestricted competition
No SOC 2 compliance for potential DoD information systems requirements
Pilot may require existing mature commercial product, not custom development
nextSteps: Assess if any team members have prior body measurement/computer vision expertise not captured in profile
Identify potential teaming partners with mature measurement technology and DoD experience
Request clarification on whether pilot accepts custom development vs. COTS only
Evaluate facility clearance and SOC 2 timeline vs. project needs
Determine if company can serve as software integrator for a hardware partner's solution

classification.summary: The Army needs a mature commercial, non‑contact system that automatically measures body and foot dimensions and translates them into recommended uniform and footwear sizes to eliminate manual bottlenecks and reduce return rates.
